events.title: Death of King Edward I of England
events.description: Edward I, known as 'Longshanks' and the 'Hammer of the Scots,' died at Burgh by Sands while marching north to campaign against Scotland. He was succeeded by his son Edward II.
events.significance: Edward's death marked the end of a reign that reshaped English law and government and brought Wales under English control. His weaker successor soon lost ground in Scotland, culminating in Bannockburn in 1314.

events.title: Execution of the Lincoln Assassination Conspirators
events.description: Four people convicted of conspiring in the assassination of President Abraham Lincoln were hanged at the Washington Arsenal: Mary Surratt, Lewis Powell, David Herold, and George Atzerodt.
events.significance: Mary Surratt became the first woman executed by the U.S. federal government. The use of a military tribunal for civilians remains a subject of legal and historical debate.

events.title: Annexation of Hawaii
events.description: President William McKinley signed the Newlands Resolution, in which the United States annexed the Republic of Hawaii. The resolution had been passed by Congress amid the Spanish-American War.
events.significance: The annexation extended U.S. territory into the Pacific and strengthened its strategic position in the region. Hawaii became a U.S. territory in 1900 and a state in 1959.

events.title: Marco Polo Bridge Incident
events.description: Fighting broke out between Chinese and Japanese troops near the Marco Polo Bridge (Lugou Bridge) southwest of Beijing, after a dispute over a missing Japanese soldier.
events.significance: The incident escalated into the Second Sino-Japanese War, which merged into World War II in the Pacific and cost millions of lives.

events.title: Construction Begins on Hoover Dam
events.description: Construction of the Hoover Dam (originally Boulder Dam) on the Colorado River began in earnest, with work starting in the Black Canyon on the Nevada-Arizona border.
events.significance: Completed in 1936, the dam was a landmark of American engineering during the Great Depression, supplying hydroelectric power and water to the Southwest and providing thousands of jobs.
